BUYER RESOURCE LIBRARY

Parrot guides for a considered beginning

Start with the decision you need to make. These resources bring buying preparation, everyday care and UK documentation checks together without treating a photograph as a current bird listing.

A practical library for choosing and caring for a parrot

Buying a parrot is a long-term decision about a particular bird, not simply a choice of colour or talking ability. Use these guides to compare species, prepare your home, understand costs and identify questions to resolve before you commit. They are general information: the right answer for an individual bird depends on its history, needs and circumstances.

Crownwing Parrots has birds across eight groups available by enquiry. This describes the range of groups, not live stock or a promise that a particular species, age or individual is available. Exact species and individual details need confirmation. Photographs in the gallery are not a stock list; ask about the actual bird you are considering.

Start with How to Buy a Parrot in the UK for the whole buyer journey, then use the questions-before-buying checklist when speaking with a seller.

Buying and choosing guides

  • How to Buy a Parrot in the UK: Complete Buyer’s Guide — work through species fit, weaning, records, questions, preparation and the first week.
  • Choosing a parrot for your home — compare routines and household needs without a “best bird” ranking.
  • Buying a parrot checklist — keep the questions and evidence you need to clarify together.
  • Preparing for a parrot — plan the home and routine before a bird arrives.

Explore the species guides and available groups, remembering that a category page or gallery image does not confirm current stock.

Care, accommodation and lifetime planning

  • Parrot ownership costs — budget for lifetime care separately from a bird’s purchase quote.
  • Parrot diet and nutrition — discuss a gradual, bird-specific feeding plan.
  • Parrot housing and enrichment — consider usable space, safety, exercise and activity.

For questions about current birds, contact Crownwing directly through the enquiry page. Before proceeding, ask for current availability and pricing for the specific individual and confirm all relevant arrangements.

UK documentation and legal checks

Some birds and situations involve CITES documents, identification, movement permits or keeper-registration rules; there is no single paperwork rule for every parrot. Read the UK CITES and parrot documentation guide and verify the actual species, origin, destination and proposed use with the relevant authority before agreeing a transaction or journey.

Other useful routes include the care library, species collection, available groups, buying enquiries, and contact.
